name: HVAC / Home Services

source.readFrom: Synthesized from established HVAC / home-services web conventions (not copied from any specific design). Add real reference images to design-library/hvac/ to refine.

character: Trust-first HVAC / home-services site built to make the phone ring. Clean and confident, blue for cooling + a warm red/orange for heating, big legible type, prominent phone number and 'Schedule Service' CTA, licensed/insured trust signals everywhere, and real technician/equipment photos. Best for HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, garage-door, pest-control and similar local home-services trades.

primary.note: A strong grotesk (Inter, Manrope, or a condensed like Oswald/Anton for headings) reads dependable. Avoid thin or decorative fonts.

scale.note: Small label above headings ('24/7 EMERGENCY SERVICE').
The phone number is a headline-weight element in the header and CTAs.

typography.notes: Big, bold, legible. The phone number is treated as a first-class heading element, not fine print. Uppercase eyebrows for urgency/credentials.

color.notes: Cool BLUE primary (trust, cooling) with a warm RED/ORANGE 'heat' accent for heating/urgency (emergency banners, hot deals) and a green for 'licensed/verified' ticks. Near-navy ink on white / pale-blue surfaces. REUSE this cool-primary + warm-accent structure; put the lead's real brand colour in the blue slot and keep a warm accent for urgency.

spacing.notes: Roomy ~64–80px sections, white cards with soft shadow, ~1200px column. Comfortable and uncluttered — trades customers scan fast.

header.note: STICKY header with a top utility strip (hours + '24/7 Emergency') and, in the main bar, the logo, nav, a bold click-to-call phone number, and a solid 'Schedule Service' button. The phone + CTA are always visible.

button.notes: Every section ends with a call or booking CTA.

card.shape: White, soft shadow, rounded; blue icon.

badges.note: Licensed · Insured · BBB · financing · warranty · brand-certified (Carrier/Trane) badges near the hero and footer.

order.layout: Sticky. Utility strip (hours + emergency line) on top; main bar: logo · nav · bold phone number · 'Schedule Service' button.

Left: eyebrow (e.g. '24/7 EMERGENCY HVAC') + big value-prop heading + one line + two CTAs (Call Now / Book Online) + a row of trust badges (Licensed, Insured, ★ reviews). Right: a real technician / HVAC-unit photo, or a short 'request service' form.
A slim band of proof: years in business, jobs completed, star rating, brand-certified logos.
Heading + a grid of service cards (AC Repair, Heating, Installation, Maintenance, Indoor Air Quality) — icon → title → one line → 'Learn more'.
Two columns: a real photo beside a checklist of differentiators (upfront pricing, same-day service, satisfaction guarantee, certified techs).
3–4 numbered steps: Book → Diagnose → Fix → Relax.
A warm-accent band with a coupon / seasonal tune-up offer and financing ('$0 down, low monthly').
A map or a list of towns/zip codes served, with a 'Not sure if we cover you? Call us' CTA.
Star rating summary + a row of real Google review cards (quote → name → town).
Full-width primary band: big 'Need service today?' heading + phone number + Book button.
Contact, hours, service area, license number, brand certifications, quick links; the phone number repeated large.

reusableArchetypes: sticky phone-CTA header with emergency strip
hero with trust badges + call/book CTAs + technician photo (or inline request form)
craftNotes: The phone number and 'Schedule Service' CTA must be visible at all times — home-services convert by call/booking.
Trust signals (licensed, insured, reviews, brand-certified, warranty, financing) appear early and often.
Use the lead's REAL technician/team/equipment photos; stock-feeling imagery kills trust.
One cool primary for calm/trust + a warm accent strictly for urgency and offers.

reuse: Use for HVAC / plumbing / electrical / roofing / and similar local home-services trades. Take the sticky phone-CTA header, trust-badge hero, service grid, offers/financing band, service-area section and review cards. Put the lead's brand colour in the blue slot, keep a warm accent for urgency, and use their real photos and real phone number, license and service area from FACTS.
